The '''2024–25 season''' was [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|121st season in existence]] and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|94th consecutive season]] in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. In addition to the [[2024–25 La Liga|domestic league]], Real Madrid participated in this season's editions of the [[2024–25 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2025 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] and the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].

As the reigning [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|European champions]], Real Madrid contested the [[2024 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] against [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]], winning 2–0 and claiming a [[List of UEFA Super Cup finals#Performances|record-breaking]] sixth title,<ref name="UEFA SC win">{{cite news|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Atalanta: Mbappé scores as Los Blancos claim Super Cup|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/0290-1b9cb774481e-880cbe608abf-1000--real-madrid-2-0-atalanta-mbappe-scores-as-los-blancos-claim/|website=UEFA.com|publisher=[[UEFA|Union of European Football Associations]]|date=14 August 2024|access-date=14 August 2024|archive-date=14 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240814213305/https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/0290-1b9cb774481e-880cbe608abf-1000--real-madrid-2-0-atalanta-mbappe-scores-as-los-blancos-claim/|url-status=live}}</ref> then went on to win the inaugural edition of the [[FIFA Intercontinental Cup]], beating [[C.F. Pachuca|Pachuca]] 3–0 in the [[2024 FIFA Intercontinental Cup final|final]],<ref name="FIFA IC win">{{cite web|title=Real Madrid beat Pachuca to win Intercontinental Cup|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/fifa-club-world-cup/articles/real-madrid-pachuca-report-final|website=FIFA.com|publisher=[[FIFA|Fédération Internationale de Football Association]]|date=18 December 2024|access-date=18 December 2024|archive-date=18 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241218190824/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/fifa-club-world-cup/articles/real-madrid-pachuca-report-final|url-status=live}}</ref> and also competed in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]] where they reached the semi-finals. With these two wins, [[Carlo Ancelotti]] conquered his 14th and 15th trophies in charge of Real Madrid, overtaking [[Miguel Muñoz]] to become the [[List of Real Madrid CF managers#Trophies|most decorated]] manager in the club's history.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ancelotti becomes the most decorated coach in Real Madrid history|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/ancelotti-18-12-2024|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=18 December 2024|access-date=18 December 2024|archive-date=18 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241218211257/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/ancelotti-18-12-2024|url-status=live}}</ref> This season also marked the end of Ancelotti's second managerial stint at the club, as he was replaced by [[Xabi Alonso]] after the conclusion of La Liga.<ref name="Carlo leaves"/><ref name="Alonso appointment"/>

This season was the first since [[2013–14 Real Madrid CF season|2013–14]] without [[Toni Kroos]], who announced his retirement in May 2024,<ref>{{cite news|last=Azzoni|first=Tales|title=Germany and Real Madrid great Toni Kroos to retire after Euro 2024|url=https://apnews.com/article/toni-kroos-retirement-real-madrid-germany-8987e119483b04a3ae6828312dbc36d1|publisher=Associated Press|date=21 May 2024|access-date=26 May 2024|archive-date=21 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521230815/https://apnews.com/article/toni-kroos-retirement-real-madrid-germany-8987e119483b04a3ae6828312dbc36d1|url-status=live}}</ref> as well as first since [[2009–10 Real Madrid CF season|2009–10]] without [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]], who departed as a free agent to Saudi Arabian club [[Al Qadsiah FC|Al-Qadsiah]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

==Summary==
===Pre-season===
On 15 December 2022, during the [[2022–23 Real Madrid CF season|2022–23]] season, Madrid announced an agreement with [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] for [[Endrick]] to join the club in July 2024, when he turns 18 years old.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Kallas|first1=Fernando|last2=Ferris|first2=Ken|title=Real Madrid agree deal to sign Brazilian 16-year-old prodigy Endrick|url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/real-madrid-agree-deal-sign-brazilian-16-year-old-prodigy-endrick-2022-12-15/|publisher=Reuters|date=15 December 2022|access-date=14 April 2024|archive-date=16 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116030835/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/real-madrid-agree-deal-sign-brazilian-16-year-old-prodigy-endrick-2022-12-15/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 21 May 2024, [[Toni Kroos]] announced that he will retire from professional football after [[UEFA Euro 2024]], thus ending his 10 seasons in the club with 23 trophies won as a Real Madrid player.<ref>{{cite news|last=Azzoni|first=Tales|title=Germany and Real Madrid great Toni Kroos to retire after Euro 2024|url=https://apnews.com/article/toni-kroos-retirement-real-madrid-germany-8987e119483b04a3ae6828312dbc36d1|publisher=Associated Press|date=21 May 2024|access-date=26 May 2024|archive-date=21 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521230815/https://apnews.com/article/toni-kroos-retirement-real-madrid-germany-8987e119483b04a3ae6828312dbc36d1|url-status=live}}</ref> On 3 June, Madrid confirmed the signing of [[Kylian Mbappé]] from [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] as a free agent, penning a five-year deal with the French superstar.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mbappé signs for Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/mbappe-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-03-06-2024|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=3 June 2024|access-date=3 June 2024|archive-date=3 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603180429/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/mbappe-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-03-06-2024|url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 June, Madrid announced the departure of the club captain [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]] after 23 years in the club and 12 seasons as a first team player, who left as Real's joint most decorated player, having won 26 titles.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Real Madrid announce Nacho exit ahead of move to Saudi Pro League side Al Qadsiah|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5589187/2024/06/25/nacho-real-madrid-saudi-transfer-complete/|publisher=The Athletic|date=25 June 2024|access-date=25 June 2024|archive-date=25 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240625220528/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5589187/2024/06/25/nacho-real-madrid-saudi-transfer-complete/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 28 June, Madrid announced the transfer of [[Joselu]] to Qatari side [[Al-Gharafa SC|Al-Gharafa]], exercising their option to acquire the rights of the player from [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] one day earlier.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Cortegana|first1=Mario|last2=Rai|first2=Guillermo|title=Joselu, Real Madrid and a strange €1.5m transfer to Qatar explained|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5593075/2024/06/28/joselu-real-madrid-qatar-transfers/|publisher=The Athletic|date=28 June 2024|access-date=29 June 2024|archive-date=29 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240629203918/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5593075/2024/06/28/joselu-real-madrid-qatar-transfers/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 17 July, [[Luka Modrić]] signed a one-year extension, staying at the club until 2025.<ref>{{cite web|last=Millar|first=Colin|title=Luka Modrić signs new one-year Real Madrid contract|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5243327/2024/07/17/luka-modric-real-madrid-contract-new/|publisher=The Athletic|date=17 July 2024|access-date=17 July 2024|archive-date=17 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240717231239/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5243327/2024/07/17/luka-modric-real-madrid-contract-new/|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, [[Lucas Vázquez]] extended his contract until 2025.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rai|first=Guillermo|title=Lucas Vázquez signs Real Madrid contract extension|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5644975/2024/07/18/lucas-vazquez-real-madrid-contract/|publisher=The Athletic|date=18 July 2024|access-date=18 July 2024|archive-date=18 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718102917/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5644975/2024/07/18/lucas-vazquez-real-madrid-contract/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 July, Madrid confirmed that Endrick would sign a six-year deal.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Endrick's unveiling|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-presentacion-de-endrick-19-07-2024|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=19 July 2024|access-date=25 July 2024|archive-date=25 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725153034/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-presentacion-de-endrick-19-07-2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

===August===
On 14 August, Madrid's season started with a 2–0 win over [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] in the [[2024 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] for their sixth [[UEFA Super Cup|European Super Cup]] title, as a tap-in from [[Federico Valverde]] was followed up by Mbappé's debut goal for the club. In doing so, Real became the [[List of UEFA Super Cup finals#Performances|most successful]] club in the competition's history, breaking a three-way tie of five victories each along with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[AC Milan|Milan]].<ref name="UEFA SC win"/> Four days later, Madrid started their league title-defence campaign at [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], as the gamed ended 1–1, with [[Rodrygo]] scoring the only goal for his team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mallorca 1–1 Real Madrid|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/mallorca-vs-real-madrid/FaIoWnjM1NM6z7o3/|publisher=The Athletic|date=18 August 2024|access-date=19 August 2024|archive-date=18 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240818233902/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/mallorca-vs-real-madrid/FaIoWnjM1NM6z7o3/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 August, strikes from Valverde and [[Brahim Díaz]], as well as the debut goal from Endrick, helped Madrid to take a 3–0 victory over [[Real Valladolid]] at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Millington|first=Adam|title=Real Madrid 3–0 Real Valladolid: Valverde, Díaz & Endrick score for hosts|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0qelyykz3qt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=25 August 2024|access-date=25 August 2024|archive-date=25 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240825220035/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0qelyykz3qt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid was held to a 1–1 away draw against [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]], as [[Vinícius Júnior]] converted his penalty to rescue one point for ''Los Blancos''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Las Palmas 1–1 Real Madrid|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/las-palmas-vs-real-madrid/Vc8rxluPUfKZAZ25/|publisher=The Athletic|date=29 August 2024|access-date=30 August 2024|archive-date=30 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240830000033/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/las-palmas-vs-real-madrid/Vc8rxluPUfKZAZ25/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===September===
Madrid opened the month with a 2–0 home win against [[Real Betis]] on 1 September, as Mbappé got on the scoresheet twice.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Real Betis|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/real-betis-vs-real-madrid/nzHArc76IUnh2QCO/|publisher=The Athletic|date=1 September 2024|access-date=1 September 2024|archive-date=1 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240901225653/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/real-betis-vs-real-madrid/nzHArc76IUnh2QCO/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 13 September, [[Andriy Lunin]] signed a new deal until 2030.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Cortegana|first1=Mario|last2=Rai|first2=Guillermo|title=Andriy Lunin signs Real Madrid contract extension until 2030|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5760291/2024/09/11/real-madrid-andiry-lunin-contract-extension/|publisher=The Athletic|date=11 September 2024|access-date=13 September 2024|archive-date=13 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240913183102/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5760291/2024/09/11/real-madrid-andiry-lunin-contract-extension/|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, Madrid returned from the [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]], winning 2–0 at [[Real Sociedad]], with Vinícius and Mbappé both scoring from the penalty spot.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Sociedad 0–2 Real Madrid|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/real-madrid-vs-real-sociedad/Cll1ugLqeCHoQ6eh/|publisher=The Athletic|date=14 September 2024|access-date=14 September 2024|archive-date=14 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240914234702/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/real-madrid-vs-real-sociedad/Cll1ugLqeCHoQ6eh/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 17 September, Madrid played their first match in the new [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] league phase format to begin their European defending champions campaign, as Mbappé, [[Antonio Rüdiger]] and Endrick scored in a 3–1 victory over [[VfB Stuttgart]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Coates|first=Charlotte|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Stuttgart: Endrick breaks record and Mbappé scores as Real Madrid seal Champions League win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/crr5l0kl81lt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=17 September 2024|access-date=17 September 2024|archive-date=18 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240918002854/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/crr5l0kl81lt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, goals from [[Dani Carvajal]], Rodrygo, Vinícius and Mbappé helped Madrid to take a 4–1 home comeback win against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid come back to extend unbeaten start|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr4xld2x24xt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=21 September 2024|access-date=22 September 2024|archive-date=22 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240922085833/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr4xld2x24xt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 September, Madrid beat [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] 3–2 at home with the help of goals from Vázquez, Mbappé and Rodrygo.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 3–2 Deportivo Alavés: Kylian Mbappé scores again|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn8yx0vrd0pt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=24 September 2024|access-date=2 October 2024|archive-date=2 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002140414/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn8yx0vrd0pt|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, Real played against [[Atlético Madrid]] at the [[Metropolitano Stadium]], as the first [[Madrid derby]] of the season ended in a 1–1 draw, with [[Éder Militão]] scoring the only goal for his team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cartwright|first=Phil|title=Atlético Madrid 1–1 Real Madrid: Hosts score late equaliser against Real after match was suspended for 20 minutes|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce3zvng1n5kt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=29 September 2024|access-date=2 October 2024|archive-date=2 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002140418/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce3zvng1n5kt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===October===
On 2 October, Madrid began the month with their first defeat of the season, a 1–0 Champions League loss to [[Lille OSC|Lille]] that also ended team's 36-match unbeaten run.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lille 1–0 Real Madrid: Holders suffer shock Champions League loss|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/crejngyw5n5t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=2 October 2024|access-date=2 October 2024|archive-date=2 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241002214551/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/crejngyw5n5t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, a home match against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] ended in a 2–0 win for Madrid, as Valverde and Vinícius got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Real Madrid win over Villarreal marred by Carvajal injury|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cevyzpg1zpzt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=5 October 2024|access-date=5 October 2024|archive-date=6 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006075732/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cevyzpg1zpzt|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, following Carvajal's long-term knee injury, Madrid extended his contract until 2026.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Dani Carvajal renews Real Madrid contract after suffering long-term knee injury|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5821957/2024/10/06/dani-carvajal-real-madrid-contract/|publisher=The Athletic|date=6 October 2024|access-date=6 October 2024|archive-date=6 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241006144828/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5821957/2024/10/06/dani-carvajal-real-madrid-contract/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 October, returning from another international break, Madrid faced [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] away from home, as Mbappé's strike from outside the box was followed up by a second-half winner by Vinícius to give their team a 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite web|last=Millington|first=Adam|title=Modrić becomes Real Madrid's oldest ever player|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cg78mx8l4kpt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=19 October 2024|access-date=19 October 2024|archive-date=5 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241105173558/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cg78mx8l4kpt|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, a header from Rüdiger alongside Vinícius' second-half hat-trick and a goal from Vázquez rescued Madrid from trailing 0–2 at half-time to prevailing 5–2 at home over Champions League opponents [[Borussia Dortmund]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rindl|first=Joe|title=Vinícius Jr scores hat-trick in stunning Real comeback win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c70zpkxqe87t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=22 October 2024|access-date=22 October 2024|archive-date=5 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241105173756/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c70zpkxqe87t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 26 October, Madrid was stunned by a 0–4 loss to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in the first [[El Clásico]] of the season. This defeat also ended Real's 42-game unbeaten streak in La Liga, just one short of equaling the league record.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rose|first=Gary|title=Real Madrid 0–4 Barcelona: Robert Lewandowski, Lamine Yamal and Raphinha score El Clásico goals|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cqjrjjrz5dgt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=26 October 2024|access-date=28 October 2024|archive-date=5 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241105173857/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cqjrjjrz5dgt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===November===
On 5 November, the first match of the month ended in another defeat for Madrid, this time losing 1–3 at home to [[AC Milan|Milan]] in the Champions League, with Vinícius scoring the only goal for his team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Emma|title=Real Madrid 1–3 AC Milan: Spaniards fall to second straight home loss|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c4gm0drjw2rt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=5 November 2024|access-date=6 November 2024|archive-date=6 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241106145834/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c4gm0drjw2rt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid took a 4–0 victory against [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], with Vinícius' second hat-trick of the season being joined by [[Jude Bellingham]]'s first goal for Real since May.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Real Madrid 4–0 Osasuna: Vinícius Júnior hits hat-trick but Éder Militão tears ACL|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn7mdm71emzt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=9 November 2024|access-date=9 November 2024|archive-date=9 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241109212850/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn7mdm71emzt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 November, goals from Mbappé, Valverde and Bellingham gave Madrid a dominant 3–0 win at [[CD Leganés|Leganés]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Coates|first=Charlotte|title=Leganés 0–3 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé and Jude Bellingham score as visitors close gap on Barca|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c78dkp0gkz0t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=24 November 2024|access-date=24 November 2024|archive-date=24 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241124210408/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c78dkp0gkz0t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid was beaten 0–2 by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the Champions League at the [[Anfield]] in their first loss against the English side since [[2008–09 Real Madrid CF season|2009]].<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Liverpool beat Real Madrid to extend perfect Champions League run|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c78dgjj1x35t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=27 November 2024|access-date=27 November 2024|archive-date=27 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127224529/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c78dgjj1x35t|url-status=live}}</ref>

===December===
On 1 December, Madrid began the month with a 2–0 victory over [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] at the Santiago Bernabéu, as Bellingham and Mbappé got on the scoresheet in the first half.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Bellingham & Mbappé score as Real Madrid beat Getafe|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c774p71xxk5t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=1 December 2024|access-date=1 December 2024|archive-date=1 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241201180156/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c774p71xxk5t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid suffered their second league defeat of the season, losing 1–2 at [[Athletic Bilbao]] in [[El Viejo Clásico]], as late Bellingham's goal was not enough to rescue a point for Real.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coates|first=Charlotte|title=Athletic Bilbao 2–1 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham scores but Real Madrid lose in La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c20602dx55nt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=4 December 2024|access-date=4 December 2024|archive-date=10 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210225308/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c20602dx55nt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 7 December, Madrid played [[Girona FC|Girona]] away from home, winning 3–0, thanks to Bellingham's fifth consecutive La Liga goal and strikes from Güler and Mbappé.<ref>{{cite web|title=Girona 0–3 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé score in La Liga win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5y485lq61nt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=7 December 2024|access-date=7 December 2024|archive-date=10 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210225404/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5y485lq61nt|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid beat Atalanta 3–2 on their pitch in the Champions league, as Mbappé, Vinícius and Bellingham scored the goals for ''Los Blancos''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mbappé scores landmark goal as Real Madrid triumph|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cql55yr1zd2t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=10 December 2024|access-date=10 December 2024|archive-date=10 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210224352/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cql55yr1zd2t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 December, Madrid was held to a 3–3 draw at [[Rayo Vallecano]], with Valverde, Bellingham and Rodrygo scoring for the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jude Bellingham scores again but Real Madrid held to draw by Rayo Vallecano in thriller|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cvgmprx5kxrt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=14 December 2024|access-date=14 December 2024|archive-date=14 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241214222737/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cvgmprx5kxrt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid were crowned as the inaugural [[FIFA Intercontinental Cup]] champions, beating [[C.F. Pachuca|Pachuca]] 3–0 in the [[2024 FIFA Intercontinental Cup final|final]] with the help of goals from Mbappé, Rodrygo and Vinícius.<ref name="FIFA IC win"/> On 22 December, Madrid ended the year with a dominant display in a 4–2 home win over [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], as Mbappé, Valverde, Rodrygo and Brahim found the back of the net for Real.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Real Madrid 4–2 Sevilla: Hosts move a point behind leaders Atlético|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c23vpzy3rnlt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=22 December 2024|access-date=22 December 2024|archive-date=22 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241222174300/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c23vpzy3rnlt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===January===
On 3 January, Madrid played their first game of the year, where late goals from Modrić and Bellingham powered a 2–1 comeback win at [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Emons|first=Michael|title=Valencia 1–2 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham winner sends Real Madrid top of La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cm2m9y3v044t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=3 January 2025|access-date=4 January 2025|archive-date=4 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250104123606/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cm2m9y3v044t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid began their [[2024–25 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] campaign, beating [[Segunda Federación|fourth-tier]] [[CD Minera|Minera]] 5–0 and progressing to the round of 16, thanks to goals from Valverde and [[Eduardo Camavinga]], followed up by a brace from Güler and a finish from Modrić.<ref>{{cite web|title=Deportiva Minera 0–5 Real Madrid: Arda Güler hits two in Copa del Rey romp|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c2kx7zxx2xet|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=6 January 2025|access-date=6 January 2025|archive-date=8 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108204903/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c2kx7zxx2xet|url-status=live}}</ref> On 9 January, goals from Bellingham and Rodrygo, as well as an own goal, helped Madrid win the [[2025 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] semi-final against Mallorca 3–0 and reach the [[2025 Supercopa de España final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 3–0 Mallorca: Jude Bellingham scores to help Real reach Super Cup final|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5y7n7llk5gt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=9 January 2025|access-date=10 January 2025|archive-date=10 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250110204224/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c5y7n7llk5gt|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid suffered another big defeat in El Clásico this season, losing 2–5 to Barcelona in the Spanish Super Cup final, as the only goals for the team came from Mbappé and Rodrygo.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–5 Barcelona: Hansi Flick's side win 15th Spanish Cup|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj91ljy0r0xt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=12 January 2025|access-date=15 January 2025|archive-date=14 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114215254/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj91ljy0r0xt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 16 January, goals from Mbappé and Vinícius in a Copa del Rey round of 16 match against Celta Vigo led Madrid to extra time, where a brace from Endrick was joined by Valverde's strike to give Real a 5–2 home win and qualification for the next round.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 5–2 Celta Vigo: Hosts need extra-time to reach last eight|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c70kwern9x3t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=16 January 2025|access-date=16 January 2025|archive-date=17 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250117120957/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c70kwern9x3t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid got a 4–1 win over Las Palmas with the help of two goals from Mbappé followed by strikes from Brahim and Rodrygo to move top of La Liga. The match also marked [[David Alaba]]'s return from his [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL injury]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Las Palmas: Hosts score four as Real come from behind|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cyv47v9rn04t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=19 January 2025|access-date=19 January 2025|archive-date=19 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119183031/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cyv47v9rn04t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 22 January, Rodrygo's and Vinícius' braces with a goal from Mbappé helped Madrid to take a crushing 5–1 victory over [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]] in the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Emma|title=Real Madrid 5–1 Red Bull Salzburg: Crushing win boosts holders' Champions League hopes|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c9vmm3wn28jt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=22 January 2025|access-date=22 January 2025|archive-date=22 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250122225507/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c9vmm3wn28jt|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Mbappé scored his first hat-trick for the club, netting all three goals in a 3–0 win at Real Valladolid.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Real Valladolid 0–3 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé hits hat-trick to send Real four points clear|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cq6g7zgm00mt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=25 January 2025|access-date=25 January 2025|archive-date=25 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125223104/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cq6g7zgm00mt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 29 January, Madrid faced [[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]] on the road in the Champions League and beat them 3–0 with Rodrygo's brace and a goal from Bellingham, qualifying to the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Knockout phase play-offs|knockout phase play-offs]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Emma|title=Real miss out on top eight despite beating Brest|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckg7j4qjl0dt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=29 January 2025|access-date=29 January 2025|archive-date=29 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250129222519/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckg7j4qjl0dt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===February===
On 1 February, Madrid started the month with their third league defeat of the season, losing 0–1 away to Espanyol.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coates|first=Charlotte|title=Espanyol 1–0 Real Madrid: La Liga leaders suffer third La Liga defeat|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy9lnyqy9l7t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=1 February 2025|access-date=1 February 2025|archive-date=1 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250201221557/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy9lnyqy9l7t|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid progressed to the Copa del Rey semi-finals over Leganés, as goals from Modrić and Endrick combined with an [[Association football#Duration and tie-breaking methods|injury time]] winner from [[Real Madrid Castilla|academy]]'s [[Gonzalo García (footballer, born 2004)|Gonzalo García]] gave Real a 3–2 victory.<ref>{{cite web|title=Leganés 2–3 Real Madrid: Gonzalo García's late winner decides Copa del Rey quarter-final|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn0y96jklwlt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=5 February 2025|access-date=5 February 2025|archive-date=6 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250206114619/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn0y96jklwlt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 February, the second Madrid derby of the season ended in a 1–1 draw at the Bernabéu, as Mbappé's equaliser was not enough for three points against Atlético Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Real Madrid 1–1 Atlético Madrid: Kylian Mbappé scores equaliser after Julián Alvarez opener|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgmylevrjz4t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=8 February 2025|access-date=8 February 2025|archive-date=8 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250208224426/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgmylevrjz4t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 February, Madrid took on [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]], rematching the last season's Champions League quarter-finals encounter, but facing the English side in the knockout phase play-offs this time. A goal from Mbappé, as well as two late strikes from Brahim and Bellingham, helped Madrid to prevail 3–2 in the first leg for their 300th win in the competition and the first ever at City's home stadium.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Man City beaten by two late Real Madrid goals|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce8jp331p0jt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=11 February 2025|access-date=11 February 2025|archive-date=12 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250212121953/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce8jp331p0jt|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid clinch 300th European Cup win|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/el-real-madrid-alcanza-las-300-victorias-en-la-copa-de-europa-11-02-2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=11 February 2025|access-date=11 February 2025|archive-date=12 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250212130941/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/el-real-madrid-alcanza-las-300-victorias-en-la-copa-de-europa-11-02-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid lost points for the third time in a row, drawing 1–1 at Osasuna with a goal from Mbappé.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coates|first=Charlotte|title=Osasuna 1–1 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham sent off as La Liga leaders held|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c4g7xyzq6zjt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=15 February 2025|access-date=15 February 2025|archive-date=15 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250215173342/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c4g7xyzq6zjt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 February, Mbappé's hat-trick gave Madrid a 3–1 win against Champions League knockout phase play-offs opponents Manchester City, sending the team to the round of 16 with a 6–3 victory over two legs.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Manchester City (Agg 6–3): Kylian Mbappé's stunning hat-trick dumps City out|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/clyne5v9j7pt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=19 February 2025|access-date=19 February 2025|archive-date=19 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219223320/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/clyne5v9j7pt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Girona was beaten 2–0 at the Bernabéu with the help of goals from Modrić and Vinícius.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coates|first=Charlotte|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Girona: Stunning Luka Modrić strike helps send Real second|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj0q8ye8ve7t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=23 February 2025|access-date=23 February 2025|archive-date=23 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223222851/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj0q8ye8ve7t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 26 February, a lone goal from Endrick was enough for a 1–0 win in the Copa del Rey semi-finals first leg at Real Sociedad.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Endrick scores as Real Madrid beat Real Sociedad in Copa del Rey first leg|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgr20wk275jt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=26 February 2025|access-date=26 February 2025|archive-date=26 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250226224821/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cgr20wk275jt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===March===
On 1 March, Madrid suffered a 1–2 loss at Real Betis, with Brahim scoring the only goal for his team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Real Betis 2–1 Real Madrid: Isco nets winner against former club|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c2045qrgp2pt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=1 March 2025|access-date=1 March 2025|archive-date=1 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250301194553/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c2045qrgp2pt|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, the first leg of the Champions League round of 16 against Atlético Madrid ended in a 2–1 Madrid derby win at home, as Rodrygo and Brahim got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=Salley|first=Emily|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Atlético Madrid: Brahim Díaz nets winner in derby meeting|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c86ppej278jt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=4 March 2025|access-date=4 March 2025|archive-date=4 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250304221212/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c86ppej278jt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 9 March, Mbappé and Vinícius scored one goal each, combining for a 2–1 win over Rayo Vallecano.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Rayo Vallecano: Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Jr score as Real go level with Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cp8v67z5nndt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=9 March 2025|access-date=9 March 2025|archive-date=9 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250309173833/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cp8v67z5nndt|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid's 0–1 loss at Atlético Madrid in the return leg of the Champions League last-16 tie was followed by a goalless extra time and a 4–2 penalty shootout win, sending the team to the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlético Madrid 1–0 (2–2 on agg) Real Madrid: Holders through to last eight on penalties|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c757q3k944xt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=12 March 2025|access-date=12 March 2025|archive-date=12 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312232557/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c757q3k944xt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 15 March, a brace from Mbappé saw Madrid beat Villarreal 2–1 away from home.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Emma|title=Villarreal 1–2 Real Madrid: Mbappé double returns Real Madrid to La Liga summit|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c743x82415gt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=15 March 2025|access-date=15 March 2025|archive-date=15 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250315192953/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c743x82415gt|url-status=live}}</ref> Madrid returned to action on 29 March, getting a 3–2 win over Leganés at the Bernabéu with the help of brace from Mbappé and a goal from Bellingham.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mbappé scores winner as Real Madrid survive Leganés scare|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cm2ndndvdgmt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=29 March 2025|access-date=30 March 2025|archive-date=30 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250330144440/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cm2ndndvdgmt|url-status=live}}</ref>

===April===
Madrid began the month on 1 April with the second leg of the Copa del Rey semi-final against Real Sociedad. Regular time goals from Endrick, Bellingham and [[Aurélien Tchouaméni]] were followed up by Rüdiger's extra time equaliser for a 4–4 draw at home, sending the team to the [[2025 Copa del Rey final|final]] 5–4 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coates|first=Charlotte|title=Real Madrid 4–4 Real Sociedad (5–4 on aggregate): Antonio Rüdiger scores winner in Copa del Rey semi-final|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cg5d582nl4gt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=1 April 2025|access-date=1 April 2025|archive-date=1 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250401230535/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cg5d582nl4gt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid was beaten 1–2 by Valencia at home, as Vinícius scored the only goal for Real.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|title=Real Madrid 1–2 Valencia: Hugo Duro scores stoppage-time winner in La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c9qwv0rdj4gt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=5 April 2025|access-date=6 April 2025|archive-date=6 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250406190521/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c9qwv0rdj4gt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 April, Madrid was stomped 0–3 in the first leg of the Champions League quarter-final against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at the [[Emirates Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Howell|first=Alex|title=Arsenal 3–0 Real Madrid: Declan Rice scores two free-kicks as Gunners win Champions League quarter-final first|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx256773e2yt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=8 April 2025|access-date=8 April 2025|archive-date=8 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250408205841/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx256773e2yt|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, a lone goal from Camavinga sealed a 1–0 win at Alavés.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Deportivo Alavés 0–1 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé sent off as Los Blancos stay in touch with Barcelona at top|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpq77j2w94xt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=13 April 2025|access-date=14 April 2025|archive-date=14 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250414120037/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpq77j2w94xt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 16 April, Madrid got knocked out of the Champions League, losing 1–2 to Arsenal in the return leg of the quarter-final with a goal from Vinícius and 1–5 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|last=Howell|first=Alex|title=Real Madrid 1–2 Arsenal (1–5 on aggregate): Gunners win at Bernabéu to reach semi-finals|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0kx3ypledyt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=16 April 2025|access-date=16 April 2025|archive-date=16 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416213601/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0kx3ypledyt|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, late goal from Valverde gave Madrid a minimal 1–0 win against Athletic Bilbao.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 1–0 Athletic Bilbao: Federico Valverde scores 93rd-minute winner to close on Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c15vk4z8p78t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=20 April 2025|access-date=21 April 2025|archive-date=21 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250421180036/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c15vk4z8p78t|url-status=live}}</ref> On 23 April, Güler's shot outside the box helped Madrid to take a 1–0 win over Getafe.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Getafe 0–1 Real Madrid: Güler scores winner as gap narrows to leader Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn8vxexjzeet|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=23 April 2025|access-date=25 April 2025|archive-date=25 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425194125/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn8vxexjzeet|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid met Barcelona in the Copa del Rey final. A 2–2 draw in the regular time required extra time, where a late goal from ''Blaugrana'' sealed a 3–2 win and the title for them.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Barcelona 3–2 Real Madrid: Jules Koundé scores in extra time as Barca win Copa del Rey|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c3r811ypn23t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=26 April 2025|access-date=27 April 2025|archive-date=27 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250427090312/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c3r811ypn23t|url-status=live}}</ref>

===May===
On 4 May, Madrid began the month with a victory, as Güler's goal with a brace from Mbappé gave their team a 3–2 win over Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabéu.<ref>{{cite web|last=Drury|first=Sam|title=Mbappé scores twice as Real Madrid beat Celta Vigo|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cd6j9j0j9q3t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=4 May 2025|access-date=4 May 2025|archive-date=4 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250504184458/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cd6j9j0j9q3t|url-status=live}}</ref> A week later, Barcelona handed Madrid a 3–4 defeat, as Mbappé's hat-trick was not enough for points away from home. With this result, Real lost four consecutive El Clásicos of the campaign for the second time in their history.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brotherton|first=Alex|title=Barcelona 4–3 Real Madrid: Hosts win thriller despite Kylian Mbappé hat trick to move closer to title|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c62x2g9d9dgt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=11 May 2025|access-date=11 May 2025|archive-date=11 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250511150122/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c62x2g9d9dgt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 May, Madrid faced Mallorca at home, as Mbappé's goal was followed up by a late winner from Castilla's [[Jacobo Ramón]] to give his team a 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Mallorca: Hosts come from behind to beat Mallorca and make Barca wait for title|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/czx0gre55x9t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=14 May 2025|access-date=15 May 2025|archive-date=15 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250515155817/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/czx0gre55x9t|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid announced the signing of [[Dean Huijsen]] from [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], with the Spanish center-back joining the club on 1 June and signing a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Huijsen, new Real Madrid player|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/huijsen-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-17-05-2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=17 May 2025|access-date=17 May 2025|archive-date=17 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250517103136/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/huijsen-nuevo-jugador-del-real-madrid-17-05-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On 18 May, Madrid beat nine-man Sevilla 2–0 away from home with second-half goals from Mbappé and Bellingham.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rajan|first=Adwaidh|title=Sevilla 0-2 Real Madrid: Kylian Mbappé and Jude Bellingham guide Los Blancos to victory|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckg486n76k1t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=18 May 2025|access-date=19 May 2025|archive-date=19 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250519174820/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckg486n76k1t|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, Madrid and [[Carlo Ancelotti]] announced their mutual decision to part ways after the conclusion of La Liga, with the Italian coach leaving as the [[List of Real Madrid CF managers#Trophies|most decorated]] manager in the history of the club with 15 trophies.<ref name="Carlo leaves">{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Ancelotti|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-ancelotti-23-05-2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=23 May 2025|access-date=24 May 2025|archive-date=24 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250524081755/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/comunicado-oficial-ancelotti-23-05-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 May, Modrić and Ancelotti bid a farewell to the Bernabéu, as a brace from Mbappé saw Madrid beat Real Sociedad 2–0 in the season’s last league game.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rose|first=Gary|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Real Sociedad: Kylian Mbappé scores twice in season finale|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj3jxk2nrrjt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=24 May 2025|access-date=25 May 2025|archive-date=25 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250525091554/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj3jxk2nrrjt|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, Madrid announced the appointment of [[Xabi Alonso]] as their new head coach for the next three seasons, starting from 1 June.<ref name="Alonso appointment">{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Xabi Alonso|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-25-05-2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=25 May 2025|access-date=25 May 2025|archive-date=25 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250525103017/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-25-05-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On 30 May, Madrid and Liverpool announced an agreement for the transfer of [[Trent Alexander-Arnold]], with the Englishman joining the club on 1 June on a six-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexander-Arnold signs for Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/perfil-arnold-30-05-2025|date=30 May 2025|access-date=30 May 2025|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=30 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530104914/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/perfil-arnold-30-05-2025|url-status=live}}</ref> On the same day, the club announced the departure of [[Jesús Vallejo]] upon the expiration of his contract.<ref name=:2/>

===June===
On 18 June, Madrid debuted in the new format of the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]], being held to a 1–1 draw by [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] after Gonzalo García's goal.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sutcliffe|first=Steve|title=Real Madrid held by Al Hilal on Alexander-Arnold debut|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckgx7dylx0pt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=18 June 2025|access-date=18 June 2025|archive-date=19 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250619161733/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckgx7dylx0pt|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid got their first win of the tournament, beating Pachuca 3–1 with goals from Bellingham, Güler and Valverde.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=Club World Cup: Real Madrid 3–1 Pachuca - Jude Bellingham helps Los Blancos win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpvjyeggrkwt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=22 June 2025|access-date=22 June 2025|archive-date=22 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250622212634/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpvjyeggrkwt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 26 June, Madrid booked their place in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup knockout stage|knockout stage]], as Vinícius, Valverde and Gonzalo García scored to help Real top the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup Group H|group]] with a 3–0 win over Red Bull Salzburg.<ref>{{cite web|last=Jackson|first=Bobbie|title=Real Madrid beat RB Salzburg to reach CWC last 16|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpd1n7lywgnt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=26 June 2025|access-date=27 June 2025|archive-date=27 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250627161428/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpd1n7lywgnt|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, a lone goal from Gonzalo García sealed a 1–0 win over round of 16 opponents [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and progression to the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|last=Howarth|first=Matthew|title=Real Madrid 1–0 Juventus: Trent Alexander-Arnold sets up García winner as Real beat Juventus|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpvjrpnkwjlt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=1 July 2025|access-date=3 July 2025|archive-date=3 July 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250703092907/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cpvjrpnkwjlt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 5 July, Madrid met Borussia Dortmund in a match for the spot in the semi-finals, beating them 3–2 with goals from Gonzalo García, [[Fran García (footballer, born 1999)|Fran García]] and Mbappé.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kinsella|first=Nizaar|title=Mbappé scores as Real Madrid beat Dortmund to set up PSG semi-final|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c1k8zg47r3lt|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=5 July 2025|access-date=6 July 2025|archive-date=6 July 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250706083159/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c1k8zg47r3lt|url-status=live}}</ref> On 9 July, Madrid ended their season with a 0–4 loss against [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]], getting knocked out in the FIFA Club World Cup semi-finals. This match was the last for Modrić and Vázquez in a ''Los Blancos'' shirt, but also saw the returns of Carvajal and Militão from their long-term knee injuries.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|title=PSG 4–0 Real Madrid: European champions set up Club World Cup final against Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c74z0zxq825t|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=9 July 2025|access-date=9 July 2025|archive-date=9 July 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250709214016/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c74z0zxq825t|url-status=live}}</ref>
